**Summary for mainnet on 8 June 2026:**

| Client | 1 blob | 6 blobs | 12 blobs | 21 blobs | Scaling pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Reth** | 2.8 ms | 6.1 ms | 12.2 ms | 22.8 ms | Near-linear, ~1ms per blob |
| **Nethermind** | 2.0 ms | 12.6 ms | 18.3 ms | 24.0 ms | Roughly linear, low base |

| **Erigon** | 7.5 ms | 60.9 ms | 105 ms | 174 ms | Linear, ~8ms per blob |

All clients scale roughly **linearly** with blob count. Reth, Nethermind, and ethrex are the fastest (sub-30ms even at 21 blobs). Geth and Erigon are the slowest — about **3-5x slower** at high blob counts, with avg durations exceeding 170ms for 21 blobs. Besu sits in the middle with a flatter curve at higher counts.

runs.question: How did engine_getBlobs response time scale with blob count for each execution client on mainnet on 8 June 2026 (UTC)?
runs.answer:
**Chart** (the model can't render it inline but the URL is accessible):

`http://127.0.0.1:2480/api/v1/storage/files/92c003c9f7a4/a038a81c-f6df-4a83-a8f3-1ccba63731be/engine_getblobs_by_client.png`

---

**Key findings from `mainnet.int_engine_get_blobs` for 2026-06-08 (142,684 observations, 6 EL clients):**

All clients show a **near-linear increase** in avg `engine_getBlobs` duration with requested blob count, but with very different slopes:

| Client       | Avg duration @ 1 blob | Avg duration @ 21 blobs | ~Slope (ms/blob) |
|--------------|----------------------|------------------------|-----------------|
| **Nethermind**  | 0.9 ms               | 8.3 ms                 | **~0.4**        |
| **Reth**        | 2.3 ms               | 22.8 ms                | **~1.0**        |
| **ethrex**      | 2.0 ms               | 18.5 ms                | **~0.9**        |
| **Besu**        | 3.9 ms               | 72.6 ms                | **~3.5**        |
| **go-ethereum** | 6.2 ms               | 179 ms                 | **~8.6**        |
| **erigon**      | 7.5 ms               | 139 ms                 | **~6.6**        |

**Nethermind is the fastest** at every blob count and scales the most gently. **go-ethereum and erigon** have the steepest slopes — at 21 blobs they take ~180 ms and ~140 ms respectively, vs. Nethermind's ~8 ms. Besu has high variance (note the spike at 18 blobs / ~175 ms avg). The chart source is `mainnet.int_engine_get_blobs` from `xatu-cbt`.

|--------|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| MEV blocks (02:45–05:00) | 202 | 610 | **−66.9%** |

- **13.2 min** — slots 13166314→13166380 (03:43–03:56)
- **12.4 min** — slots 13166228→13166290 (03:25–03:38)
- **8.0 min** — slots 13166498→13166538 (04:19–04:27)

| Relay | Dip | Normal | % of normal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agnostic Gnosis | 17 | 71 | **23.9%** |
| EthGas | 5 | 18 | **27.8%** |
| Titan Relay | 72 | 240 | **30.0%** |

## MEV Relay Circuit Breaker Event — Dec 3-4, 2025

### Timeline

The outage wasn't sudden — it unfolded over ~10 hours:

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| **Dec 3 ~21:00** | Early signs: missed slots jump to 11, first relay delivery decline |
| **Dec 3 22:00-23:00** | Missed slots hit 19/hr, relay share drops to ~75% of blocks |
| **Dec 4 02:45** | Relay share falls to 69.6%, orphaned blocks spike to 7 |
| **Dec 4 03:00-04:00** | **Worst hour**: 77 missed slots (vs normal ~2), relay deliveries collapse |
| **Dec 4 03:45-04:00** | **Worst 15-min**: only **5 relay-delivered blocks** (vs normal ~69) |
| **Dec 4 04:00-05:00** | Slow recovery begins, 62 missed, 22 orphaned |
| **Dec 4 05:00-06:00** | Marked improvement, 20 missed, 18 orphaned |
| **Dec 4 06:00+** | Near-normal operation restored |

### Quantified Impact

**Relay-delivered blocks collapsed 92.8%** — from a normal average of **69.2 per 15 minutes** to just **5** at the 03:45 trough.

| Metric | Normal (pre-crash) | Worst 15-min (03:45) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total blocks produced (per 15 min) | ~74.4 | 55 | -26% |
| Missed slots (per 15 min) | ~0.6 | 20 | +3233% |
| Relay-delivered blocks (per 15 min) | ~69.2 | 5 | -92.8% |
| Locally-built blocks (per 15 min) | ~5.2 | 50 | +862% |
| Relay share of produced blocks | 93.0% | 9.1% | -90% |

**Per-relay worst drop (03:00-04:00 hour vs normal avg hourly):**

**Aggregate damage over the 3-hour acute window (03:00-06:00 UTC):**
- **159 missed slots** (vs ~9 expected)
- **46 orphaned blocks** (vs ~3 expected)
- Validators fell back to local block production en masse — local blocks surged from ~5/hr to **40-50/15min**

runs.question: On mainnet around December 3rd-4th, 2025, MEV relay circuit breakers were said to have tripped and relay-delivered blocks dropped sharply for a period. Identify the real window and measure the severity of the collapse.
runs.answer:
Here are the findings:

**Real window:** Degradation began **Dec 3, 2025 ~22:00 UTC**, with the acute collapse at **Dec 4, 03:00–04:59 UTC**, and recovery by **~14:00 UTC** same day.

**Severity:**
- Baseline: **274.7 relay blocks/hr** (normal)
- Trough: **77 relay blocks/hr** — a **72% collapse**
- Missed slots peaked at **77/hr** (25.7% of slots at 03:00) vs normal ~1-4/hr (<1.3%)
- 139 missed slots across the 2-hour peak window
- All major relays were affected: Titan Relay (-53%), Flashbots (-58%), Agnostic Gnosis (-57%), Aestus (-57%), BloXroute Regulated (-37%), Ultra Sound (-34%), BloXroute Max Profit (-25%)

**Chart:** `http://127.0.0.1:2480/api/v1/storage/files/7633f4dfdf3e/c8892462-4dc6-4a8c-b3cd-74fa81ee0f22/relay_collapse.png`
